definitions.gloss: to squeeze out; to wring out
definitions.explanation: To physically extract a liquid or substance by squeezing or pressing.

definitions.gloss: to eke out; to muster; to produce with great effort
definitions.explanation: To produce something — words, ideas, energy, money — through great effort, as if squeezing it out of oneself.

examples.japanese: チューブから{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To squeeze out from a tube.

examples.japanese: ぞうきんから{水|みず}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I wrung the water out of the rag.

examples.japanese: レモンから{最後|さいご}の{一滴|いってき}まで{果汁|かじゅう}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I squeezed out every last drop of juice from the lemon.

examples.japanese: {声|こえ}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I managed to squeeze out a voice.

examples.japanese: {知恵|ちえ}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}して{解決策|かいけつさく}を{考|かんが}えた。
examples.english: I racked my brains and came up with a solution.

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}りわずかな{体力|たいりょく}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}して、ゴールまで{走|はし}り{切|き}った。
examples.english: I mustered my last remaining strength and ran all the way to the finish.

notes:
A compound verb combining {絞|しぼ}る (to squeeze, to wring) and {出|だ}す (to put out, to produce). The figurative sense (sense 2) is extremely common and vivid — the image of squeezing something out of oneself with difficulty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {声|こえ}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す — to force out a voice (when one can barely speak)
- {知恵|ちえ}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す — to rack one's brains
- {勇気|ゆうき}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す — to muster courage
- {体力|たいりょく}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す — to summon one's last strength
- {涙|なみだ}を{絞|しぼ}り{出|だ}す — to squeeze out tears

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {絞|しぼ}る — to squeeze, to wring; the base verb without the 'out' nuance
- {振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る — to muster (strength, courage); emphasizes gathering from reserves
- {搾|しぼ}り{取|と}る — to squeeze out, to exploit; often has a negative connotation of extraction
